safety: These exercises are for everyday situations, like learning, work or friends. They aren't for painful experiences such as loss, abuse or health worries, or for times of crisis. If that's where you are, talk to someone you trust or a support line. You can stop at any time.

first.intro: Think of an everyday situation you keep seeing one way.
first.ask: What does it seem to say? Write it in a few words, or pick one that's close:

cards.text: It means I'm not good enough.
Everyone will think less of me.

first.own_label: My first reading (only you see this; it isn't saved)

belief.label: How much do you believe this reading right now?

upset.label: How upsetting does it feel right now?

control.question: Can you do something about the situation itself?

items.title: Other explanations
items.prompt: What else could explain what happened?

cards.text: It was harder than it looked.
I didn't have what I needed this time.
It's one moment, not the whole picture.

items.title: A friend's view
items.prompt: If a friend told you this about themselves, what would you say to them?
items.support: It makes sense that this bothers you. That isn't something you need to talk yourself out of.

cards.text: That doesn't sound like the whole story.
You're being harder on yourself than on anyone else.

items.title: Later on
items.prompt: In a month, what will probably matter about this?

cards.text: Most of it will have faded.
It may still matter, and that's real.

sort.intro: Place each reading where it fits best. More than one can fit, and your first reading can stay where it is.

close.none_kept: None of the readings fit right now. That's an honest answer too.
close.first_self: It still feels like it fits. You can keep it alongside the other readings that fit.
close.first_situation: Your first reading still fits. That's a real outcome: sometimes the first reading is right.
close.control: You said you can do something about this. Changing how you see it isn't the goal then; planning a step might help more.
